messages:
michael: Quick heads-up — saw a ~40% drop in prefix cache hit-rate on structured-output RAG sessions after the kernel swap last night. p95 up ~120ms on those flows. Anyone seen this shape before? :thinking:

anya: Ugh, that's bad. Do you have the small telemetry slice? per-route hit-rate + sample convo ids would help.

michael: Pasted a short snapshot from the last 24h (filtered to the RAG/structured route):
```
prefix_cache.hitrate: 0.42
kernel.version: 2.1.5
previous.kernel.version: 2.1.4
avg.tokens.per.prefix: 28
median.response.latency.p95: +120ms
workload.tag: rag-structured-long
note: spike aligns with rollout @02:17 UTC
```

kevin: Two quick guesses: (1) kernel swap changed batching/coalescing timing which affected prefix warmup ordering, (2) key fragmentation — are we hashing any ephemeral fields into the prefix key?

sara: I ran a tiny probe on a staging trace — structured outputs often include tool metadata and request IDs embedded in the prefix JSON. If those are part of the key, reuse will tank. Example we saw:
```
prefix_blob: {"user_message": "...", "tool_call": {"id": "req-7c3f"}, "meta": {"ts": 167...}}
# current key: sha256(prefix_blob)
```

kevin: Right — that explains it. In chat plain-text flows the prefix is small and stable, so hit-rate stays high. For structured RAG the prefix is more semantically identical but syntactically noisy.

michael: So options: normalize JSON before hashing (strip ephemeral fields + sort keys), or change key strategy to use a fingerprint over normalized token sequence. Any perf tradeoffs?

anya: Normalizing helps logically, but adds CPU overhead at cache lookup time. We should benchmark: normalization cost vs tokenization cost saved by higher hit-rate.

raj: Proposed quick canary: strip known ephemeral fields at proxy layer for 1h on a subset of pods, keep kernel 2.1.5 unchanged. Compare hit-rate + CPU. I can push a non-breaking proxy filter.

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted for tag=canary/prefix-normalize-2026-03-18 to env=prod-canary (10% traffic). CI: pass, rollout started. :rocket:

michael: Live results after 1h (canary 10%):
```
baseline.hitrate (rest of prod): 0.43
canary.hitrate: 0.68
canary.cpu.delta: +4.7%
canary.p95.latency: -80ms vs baseline
error.rate: no change
```

sara: Nice. So normalization wins for this workload — big hit-rate uplift and latency improvement despite CPU bump.

kevin: Looks like kernel swap originally disturbed batching ordering, making warming/eviction patterns worse for noisy keys. Normalization reduces key cardinality, so steady-state batching and prefix reuse both benefit.

anya: We should still double-check other workloads: completions-only and short-chat. Normalizing might increase collisions for some rare cases where ephemeral fields matter to semantics.

raj: Agreed — I'll expand canary to 25% with a conservative whitelist: only apply normalization for routes tagged rag-structured and rag-long. Rollback button ready.

michael: Action items:
- raj: widen canary to 25% and run 6h telemetry job (hitrate, cpu, p95)
- kevin: PR to move normalization into fast-path C++ module (reduce CPU)
- anya: run offline benchmark of normalization cost vs tokenization for 3 payload sizes
- sara: add unit test that detects ephemeral fields and verifies normalization idempotence

kevin: I'll open the PR today. We should also add a small metrics probe to detect sudden key cardinality jumps post-kernel changes.

michael: Good catch everyone. Let's sync up after the 6h run and decide full rollout. :thumbsup:
